claims.statement: Asana issues personal access tokens (PATs): long-lived tokens a user generates in the Asana developer console and uses to authenticate requests to the Asana REST API.

sources.supports: PATs are long-lived tokens allowing programmatic authentication to the API and should be stored securely.
A personal access token (PAT) contains your security credentials for the Asana platform.

claims.statement: A PAT is passed to the API like an OAuth access token, in the Authorization header as a Bearer token.

sources.supports: Personal access tokens should be used similarly to OAuth access tokens when accessing the API (i.e., passing them in the `Authorization` header).

claims.statement: Asana states its API tokens, including personal access tokens, should be treated as opaque and that token formats may change without notice; the documentation states no prefix, alphabet or length for a PAT.

sources.supports: Asana API tokens should be treated as opaque. Token formats may change without notice. This applies to any Asana API tokens, including: personal access tokens, service account tokens, and both OAuth refresh tokens and access tokens.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Candidate is not researched beyond existence: the format (prefix, alphabet, length, checksum) is not recorded and has not been researched by research-family.

The documentation says tokens are opaque and formats may change. Is any literal prefix, alphabet or length published anywhere on an official Asana page? Until one is found, attribution of a PAT from string shape alone is not supported and context (Authorization header, a developer-console token) is the only documented signal.

Task, project, user and workspace GIDs are documented as globally unique object identifiers (FAQ: "What does GID mean?"). Their digit-string shape is not recorded here; research-family should record them as benign siblings (public identifiers) so a bare numeric ID is never attributed as a token.

Lead only, not a claim: one open-source scanner rule artifact (trufflesecurity/trufflehog at 59e3b04e820c4cad30462696ac497853a5f7679c, pkg/detectors/asanapersonalaccesstoken/asanapersonalaccesstoken.go line 28, read 2026-10-04) treats a digits/digits(/digits)-colon-alphanumeric shape near the word "asana" as a personal access token. No second artifact by a different maintainer was found (no Asana rule in the other rule sets checked), so tool-corroborated is not met and Asana says tokens are opaque; no structure is recorded.
